resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination and USLHS give 1878; LighthouseFriends gives 1877. The story gives 1877 or 1878.
LighthouseFriends: 1871. The nomination: 1872. The story gives both.
LighthouseFriends: 1905. The nomination: 1906. The story gives 1906 and notes 1905.
Nomination: 1830. LighthouseFriends: 1831. Only relevant to the Lewis anecdote; the story gives both.
LighthouseFriends: the bell was tolled once every ten seconds. The nomination: struck once every ten minutes. Not resolved by any source read.
The nomination, USLHS and LighthouseFriends place a fourth-order Fresnel lens in the tower from 1854. The Lighthouse Directory says a fourth-order lens installed after 1935 is in use. Not resolved.

ALF: back-to-back storms destroyed the footbridge and harmed the piers. LighthouseFriends and the Directory: the same storms damaged the oil house and the concrete base. Both may be true; the story reports both.
The record's 2009 nrhp_listed is not verified; the nomination form was received 25 August 2009. The listing date was not read from the sources.
The Board's 1896 entry says a 1,000-pound fog bell was set up (the scan's OCR reads '1^000'pound'); LighthouseFriends gives 1,048 pounds. The story gives both.
LighthouseFriends: tolled once every ten seconds. The nomination: a single blow every ten minutes in foggy weather. Already listed; the story states both.

The ALF article (23 July 2026) says two temporary staircases were installed; the Friends' 2026 page and LighthouseFriends say three new staircases. The story gives the ALF account and notes the other count.

The nomination's Section 7 says the 1871 dwelling was built about 0.1 mile west of its present site; its Section 8 says the 1872 dwelling was built on the old foundation and moved about 200 feet east in 1897. The story follows Section 8 and does not repeat the 0.1-mile figure.

notes_for_editor: Records: the NRHP nomination (2009) is digitised and was read in full (Section 7 and 8). The brief's characteristic F G agrees with the nomination's 'fixed green'; the nomination's 'visible for 12 miles in clear weather' does not say nautical or statute miles, so the story repeats it unitless and records no range_nm (check the Light List). The brief's tower entry (cast iron built 1771) is wrong and is corrected. The 'Storm damage' chapter rests on ALF and the Friends; LighthouseFriends and the Directory describe the January 2024 damage differently, and both versions are stated. Keeper dates are from the USLHS roster (printed exactly). LighthouseFriends' keeper list matches the USLHS spans, except that it omits Elias Tarlton (1784-1793), which USLHS lists; the roster keeps that line and cites USLHS. The Board's 1896 entry (scan p. 53) reads '1^000'pound' in OCR; the story reads it as 1,000 pounds and the evidence quote matches the OCR form. The Board's 1897 entry (scan p. 295) says only 'The dwelling was moved to a new site'; the 200-foot distance and the artillery battery come from the nomination. Tour terms are the Friends' listing as of 2026-10-22; fees and the child-height rule may change. 'Access level restricted' is a judgement: the tower sits on an active Coast Guard station, and tours are by reservation only. National Register listing date unverified (nomination received 2009). The Lewis passage is quoted by LighthouseFriends from his 1842 report; the original report was not read. Overnight stays were not checked, so stay is omitted rather than set to null. Connie Small's 1986 book is cited by its title only; no passages are quoted from it. The Fort Constitution 1961 deactivation and state transfer come from the nomination only.
